7 12-12-2024 Heard Mr. Jagjit Roshan, learned Advocate for the appellant, Mr. Binod Bihari Singh, learned A.P.P for the Respondent-State and Mr. Gagandev Yadav, learned Advocate for the informant.

2. This appeal has been filed on behalf of the appellant under Section 374(2) read with Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 against the judgment of conviction dated 12.02.2024 and the order of sentence dated 17.02.2024 rendered by the learned Additional District & Patna High Court CR.

APP (DB) No.338 of 2024(7) dt.12-12-2024 Sessions Judge-VII-Cum-Special Judge,
POCSO, Madhubani in Sessions Trial No. 120 of 2024 arising out of Harlakhi P.S. Case No. 115 of Amar Yadav @ Amar Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 12 December, 2024

sentences.text:
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43435687/
1 2021, whereby the appellant has been convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 417 and 376 of Indian Penal Code (in short 'IPC') and Section 4 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of twenty years and a fine of Rs. 15,000/- and, in default of payment of fine, the appellant shall have further to undergo simple imprisonment for six months for the offence under Section 4 of POCSO Act read with Section 376 of IPC as per provision of Section 42 of POCSO Act and the appellant has been further sentenced to undergo imprisonment for a term of one year for the offence punishable under Section 417 of IPC and all the sentences have been directed to run concurrently.
3.

Learned Advocate for the appellant, at the outset, submitted that this Court has already admitted the present appeal and the appellant prays for grant of bail and for suspension of sentence imposed by the learned trial court till final disposal of the appeal.
4. Learned Advocate for the appellant mainly submitted that the prosecution has failed to prove that the victim was minor on the date of occurrence.

In fact, during the course Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.338 of 2024(7) dt.12-12-2024 of deposition, none of the prosecution witnesses have produced any documentary evidence with regard to the age of the victim.
Learned Advocate for the appellant has supplied the copy of the deposition of the prosecution witnesses.
He referred to the same and thereafter contended that the victim has deposed in examination-in-chief that she studied up to Standard VIII in Middle School, Gangaur.
It has been pointed out by learned Advocate that the said deposition was given by her before the Court in February, 2023.
It is further submitted that during cross-examination, in paragraph-6, the victim has admitted that in the year 2021 she left the school.
Further, she has admitted that after passing Standard VII, she appeared in Standard VIII exam.
Thereafter, learned Advocate has referred to the deposition given by PW-5, who is father of the victim.
It is contended that the said witness has stated that his daughter studied up to Standard IX and he had given the certificate of Standard VIII as well as Aadhar Card to the police.

However,
none of the prosecution witnesses have produced any documentary evidence at the time of giving deposition before the Court.
5. Learned Advocate, at this stage, submits that the trial court has placed reliance upon Exhibit-8 which was Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.338 of 2024(7) dt.12-12-2024 produced after the deposition of the prosecution witnesses was over.

It has been pointed out from the trial court records that after the deposition of the prosecution witnesses was over, application was submitted to the Court along with the Matriculation Certificate of the victim in which the date of birth of the victim is shown as 13.05.2006.
It is further submitted that the said certificate was issued by concerned School Board on 31.03.2022.

Thus, it has been contended that when the prosecution witnesses have deposed before the Court in the year 2023, the aforesaid certificate was available despite which nobody produced the same before the Court and after the evidence was closed, such type of application was given.

It has been pointed out that said application was opposed by the defense despite which the trial court passed the order on 10.11.2023 and, surprisingly, the said document has been exhibited and simply relying upon the same it has been determined by the trial court that the victim was minor and was less than 16 years of age on the date of occurrence.

Amar Yadav @ Amar Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43435687/
2 6.

entities.text: Amar Yadav @ Amar Kumar vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At this stage, learned Advocate has also referred to the deposition given by PW-8, the doctor who had examined the victim.
It is submitted that, as per the opinion given by the Medical Board about the age, the victim was between 17-18 Patna High Court CR.

Learned Advocate, therefore, contended that prosecution has failed to prove that the victim was minor on the date of occurrence and Exhibit-8, which has been produced before the Court after the deposition of the prosecution witnesses was over, cannot be looked into.
Even the opportunity to cross-examine the concerned witness with regard to the said certificate was not provided to the defense.

Learned Advocate, therefore, urged that trial court has committed grave error while recording conviction under the provisions of POCSO Act as well as under Section 376(3)
of IPC.
7.
It is contended that the medical evidence also does not support the allegation levelled by the victim against the appellant.

It is also submitted that from paragraph-5 of cross- examination of PW-7, Investigating Officer, it is revealed that the Investigating Agency did not collect any document with regard to the abortion of the victim.
Thus, the said allegation is also not supported by any evidence.
Learned Advocate, therefore, urged that appellant be released on bail.

8. On the other hand, learned Advocate for the informant has opposed the prayer for grant of bail by contending that from Exhibit-8 produced by the prosecution it is clear that victim was minor on the date of occurrence.

As per provisions Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.338 of 2024(7)
dt.12-12-2024 contained in the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 and the Rules framed thereunder, matriculation certificate of the victim is required to be looked into and the trial court has rightly placed reliance upon the said document.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Thus, when the victim was minor on the date of occurrence, no error has been committed by the trial court by passing the impugned judgment and order.
Learned Advocate, therefore, urged that appellant may not be released on bail.
9. Learned A.P.P. for the Respondent-State has also supported the submissions canvassed by learned Advocate for the informant.

10. Having heard learned Advocates appearing for the parties and having gone through the materials placed on record, deposition of the prosecution witnesses as well as the trial court records,
it would, prima facie, emerge that there is a gross delay in lodging the FIR and, in fact, written complaint has been submitted by the victim.

Further, PW-2 (victim) has admitted in paragraph-13 of the cross-examination that the written report/complaint was written by somebody else and she does not know about the name and address of the said person.
It further transpires from the record that PW-2 (victim) has specifically deposed in paragraph-1 itself that she had studied up to Standard Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.338 of 2024(7) dt.12-12-2024 VIII in Middle school, Gangaur
and during cross-examination in paragraph-6 she has admitted that she left the school in the year 2021.
She has further admitted in paragraph-13 that she passed Standard VII examination and thereafter studied up to Standard VIII.
Further PW-5, who is father of the victim, has stated that his daughter studied up to Standard IX and he provided certificate of Standard VIII and Aadhar Card to the police.
However, it is pertinent to note at this stage that none of the prosecution witnesses had produced any documentary evidence with regard to the age of the victim.

Amar Yadav @ Amar Kumar vs The State Of Bihar on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43435687/
3 10.1)

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further required to be observed, at this stage, that the aforesaid witnesses have deposed before the Court in February as well as May, 2023.
Even evidence of the prosecution was closed in August, 2023, despite which the documentary evidence with regard to the age of the victim was not produced before the Court.

Surprisingly, after the evidence of the prosecution was closed, an application was given to the Court with copy of the certificate of matriculation examination wherein the date of birth of the victim has been shown as 13.05.2006.
The said certificate was issued by the concerned School Board on 31.03.2022.

Thus, doubt has been raised by the learned Advocate for the appellant that though the said Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.338 of 2024(7) dt.12-12-2024 certificate was available since March, 2022, why the same was not produced before the Court by any of the prosecution witnesses in May, 2023 at the time of their deposition.

Further, the said allegation was opposed by the defense despite which on 10th November, 2023, the trial court passed the order and the said document was taken on record vide Exhibit-8.
11.

From the material placed on record and the evidence led by the prosecution, prima facie, we are of the view that learned Advocate for the appellant is right in submitting that the prosecution has failed to prove that the victim was minor on the date of occurrence.

12. Further, the doctor (PW-8), who had examined the victim, has specifically deposed that,
according to Radiological finding given by Medical Board, the age of the victim is between 17-18 years.
Further, it has been deposed by the said doctor that, according to present physical and pathological examination, no medical evidence of sexual assault was found at the time of examination.
The said doctor has further admitted during cross-examination in paragraph-10 that opinion regarding age may vary by two years on either side.
13. Further, it is revealed from paragraph-8 of deposition of PW-2 (victim) that she did not inform her parents Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.338 of 2024(7) dt.12-12-2024 with regard to the abortion and, for the first time, she disclosed before her parents when the written complaint was given in the police station,
whereas PW-4, who is mother of the victim, has admitted during cross-examination that after the abortion of the victim, the treatment was given by Dr. Rambabu.
However, she does not know about the address of the said doctor.
Even, the Investigating Officer (PW-7) has admitted in paragraph-5 of cross-examination that there is no document available in the case diary with regard to the abortion of the victim.
14. Even otherwise, prima facie, there are major contradictions and inconsistencies in the deposition of the prosecution witnesses.
We are, therefore, of the view that the request made by the appellant for grant of bail and for suspension of sentence till final disposal of the appeal requires consideration.

15. Accordingly, appellant is ordered to be released on bail during pendency of the present appeal on executing bond of Rs. 15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand) and upon furnishing two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional District & Sessions Judge-VII-Cum-Special Judge, POCSO, Madhubani in Sessions Trial No. 120 of 2024 arising out of Harlakhi P.S. Case No. 115 of 2021 and the Patna High Court CR.

18. Realisation of fine shall also remain stayed during the pendency of this appeal.
